question: What are the longitudinal muscular bands running along the length of the colon called?
explanation: Taeniae coli are three distinct longitudinal bands of smooth muscle visible on the outer surface of the colon, responsible for creating its segmented appearance. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary physiological role of the large intestine regarding fluid balance?

options.A: Filtering metabolic toxins directly from the bloodstream
options.B: Reabsorbing large volumes of water from chyme to form solid feces
options.C: Producing daily gastric acid for mechanical digestion
options.D: Secreting digestive enzymes to break down complex proteins

explanation: As waste material moves through the colon, the mucosa reabsorbs water and electrolytes, converting liquid chyme into formed stool. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why must a nurse auscultate bowel sounds before performing abdominal palpation?

options.A: Auscultation is required to lubricate the lower abdominal wall muscles
options.B: Standard protocol dictates upper body assessment must precede lower body inspection
options.C: Palpation can alter natural bowel motility and invalidate auscultation findings
options.D: Palpation immediately triggers a massive release of gastric acid

explanation: Deep or even light palpation stimulates peristalsis, which can artificially increase or distort bowel sounds if done first. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which diagnostic modality is considered the gold standard for visualizing the entire colonic mucosa?
explanation: Colonoscopy allows direct visualization of the entire large intestine and provides opportunities for tissue biopsy and polyp removal. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which pathological feature distinguishes Crohn's disease from ulcerative colitis?

options.A: Transmural involvement and skip lesions throughout the GI tract
options.B: Absence of any risk for developing fistulas or strictures
options.C: Exclusive restriction of inflammation to the rectal mucosa
options.D: Direct bacterial infection caused by specific parasite exposure

explanation: Crohn's disease is characterized by deep, transmural inflammation and non-continuous patches of diseased tissue known as skip lesions. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient presenting with continuous bloody diarrhea, rectal urgency, and inflammation limited strictly to the inner lining of the large colon is most likely experiencing what condition?
explanation: Ulcerative colitis consistently affects the mucosal layer of the colon and rectum in a continuous pattern, classically presenting with bloody stools. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: In which quadrant of the abdomen is pain most characteristically localized during an acute episode of diverticulitis?
explanation: Because diverticula are most prevalent in the sigmoid and descending colon, inflammation typically manifests as left lower quadrant abdominal pain. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary mechanical factor contributing to the development of colonic diverticula?

options.A: Hypersecretion of hydrochloric acid within the proximal large bowel
options.B: Elevated intraluminal pressure from chronic straining against low-fiber stool
options.C: Congenital weakness in the muscularis mucosa present at birth
options.D: Chronic bacterial overgrowth in the cecal appendix

explanation: Low-fiber diets produce small, hard stools requiring high colon pressure to propel, pushing the mucosa outward through weak spots in the muscle wall. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h4)

question: What kind of disorder is irritable bowel syndrome classified as?

options.A: An autoimmune condition causing transmural bowel necrosis
options.B: A malignant neoplasm originating from the colonic crypt cells
options.C: A functional gastrointestinal disorder without structural tissue damage
options.D: An acute bacterial infection requiring immediate surgical resection

explanation: IBS does not cause inflammation, ulcers, or structural damage; instead, it disrupts normal bowel function and motility. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which clinical strategy is typically prioritized first when establishing a diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome?

options.A: Scheduling prophylactic surgical colectomy to prevent perforation
options.B: Initiating immediate total parenteral nutrition to rest the bowel
options.C: Excluding structural or inflammatory bowel diseases through diagnostic tests
options.D: Administering high-dose systemic corticosteroids for inflammation

explanation: Because IBS shares symptoms with organic diseases like IBD and cancer, clinicians must rule out these conditions before confirming an IBS diagnosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h5)

question: What type of precursor lesion is most commonly associated with the development of colorectal cancer?
explanation: Adenomatous polyps have malignant potential and can undergo dysplastic changes leading to colorectal adenocarcinoma over time. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is early-stage colorectal cancer frequently undetected without routine screening programs?

options.A: Routine blood tests consistently mask the presence of early mucosal masses
options.B: The early stages of the disease typically do not produce noticeable symptoms
options.C: Tumors in the distal colon dissolve naturally before causing obstruction
options.D: Early malignant cells rapidly migrate out of the colon into the skin

explanation: Early colorectal cancers and polyps are usually silent, highlighting why screening tests like colonoscopies are vital for early detection. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which condition is a frequent mechanical cause of large bowel obstruction?
explanation: Tumor growth from colorectal cancer is one of the most common mechanical obstructions of the large intestine. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary clinical danger associated with prolonged, untreated large bowel obstruction?

options.A: Rapid development of permanent iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Bowel ischemia, necrosis, and subsequent perforation
options.C: Total cessation of all normal pancreatic enzyme secretion
options.D: Massive systemic absorption of vitamins and minerals

explanation: High intraluminal pressure cuts off blood flow to the bowel wall, leading rapidly to tissue death and perforation into the peritoneal cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the expected, healthy appearance of a newly created surgical stoma during initial postoperative assessments?
explanation: A healthy stoma is rich in blood supply and should always appear pink or red and moist. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h8)

question: A nurse assesses a patient's newly created ileostomy 6 hours post-surgery and notes that the stoma tissue appears dark purple and dry. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Irrigate the stoma tubing with sterile normal saline solution
options.B: Notify the surgeon immediately due to suspected compromised blood supply
options.C: Document the finding as a normal expected inflammatory response
options.D: Apply an ice pack directly to the stoma to reduce local swelling

explanation: A dark purple or black stoma indicates ischemia or necrosis resulting from impaired blood circulation, requiring urgent surgical evaluation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h8)
